details.title: Morphology
details.content: Spherical cells, grape-like clusters.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Aerobic/facultative, smooth colonies (golden/white/lemon).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Strongest among nonspores; high salt tolerance; 90% penicillin-resistant.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Coagulase, SPA, staphylolysin, leukocidin, exfoliative toxin, TSST-1, enterotoxin.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Local pyogenic infections (furuncle, carbuncle), bacteremia, SSSS, TSS, food poisoning.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Hygiene, sensitive antibiotics.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Spherical cells, arranged in chains.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Facultative anaerobe, requires enriched media; classified by hemolysis (α, β, γ).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Weak; sensitive to normal antiseptics, penicillin, and erythromycin.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Hyaluronidase, SK, SD, Pyrogenic exotoxin, Streptolysin, M protein.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Sore throat, pyoderma, erysipelas, scarlet fever, rheumatic fever.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Penicillin (first choice); timely treatment of primary infection.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Short rods, mostly possess peritrichous flagella & pili.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Lactose (+); forms pink, large colonies on SS medium.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Susceptible to standard disinfectants; easily develops opportunistic drug resistance.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Pili, LT & ST enterotoxins, Shiga toxin.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Extraintestinal (UTI, septicemia); Gastroenteritis via ETEC, EPEC, EHEC, EIEC, EAggEC.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Stool/urine culture on SS agar; fluid management and antibiotics.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Short rods; possess pili, no flagella.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Lactose (-); colorless, small colonies on SS medium.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Weak, sensitive to acid; easily develops drug resistance.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Pili, strong endotoxin, Shiga exotoxin (Stx).

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Bacillary dysentery (acute and chronic).

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Manage dehydration; antibiotics; SD vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Rods; possess pili and mostly peritrichous flagella.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Lactose (-); colorless colonies on SS medium.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Easily killed by heat and chemical disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Pili, endotoxin, enterotoxin; multiplies inside macrophages.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Gastroenteritis, Enteric (Typhoid) fever, Septicemia; carrier state in gallbladder.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Widal test; antibiotics; persistent cellular immunity post-recovery.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Short, curved (comma); single polar flagellum.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Facultative anaerobic; requires alkaline environment (pH 8.5-9.5); cultured on TCBS.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Weak; sensitive to acid/drying; dies at 100℃ in 2 minutes.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Flagella (penetration), pili (adhesion), strong Cholera Toxin (ctx).

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Cholera (severe diarrhea/rice water stools).

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Early diagnosis, quarantine, rapid rehydration, tetracycline/chloromycetin, vaccination.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Slender bacilli; terminal round spore ('drum-stick').

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate anaerobic.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Very strong; spores survive boiling, killed only by autoclaving at 121℃ under pressure.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Tetanospasmin (neurotoxin blocking inhibitory neurotransmitter release).

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Tetanus (lockjaw, spastic paralysis, severe muscle spasms).

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Debridement, TAT injection, penicillin, DPT vaccine (toxoids).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Large, rectangular bacilli; subterminal spore; capsule, non-motile.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Anaerobic; 'stormy fermentation' in milk medium.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Strong resistance due to spores.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: α, β, ε, ι exotoxins (primarily α toxin) and enterotoxin.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Gas gangrene; mild, self-limiting food poisoning.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Debridement, hyperbaric oxygen, antitoxin, antimicrobial therapy.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Bacilli; subterminal oval spore ('tennis racket'); flagella present.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate anaerobic.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Spores highly resistant; toxin is heat-labile.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Botulinum neurotoxin blocks release of acetylcholine.

details.title: Clinical
details.content: Botulism (food poisoning/infant botulism); flaccid paralysis.

details.title: Treatment
details.content: Heat food thoroughly, administer anti-toxin, antibiotic therapy if infected.
